Business insurance

Insurance Solutions for Small and Medium Businesses in Kenya

A small business can be set back by a single bad day: a fire in the stockroom, a customer who slips, an employee injured on the job. SME insurance brings the covers that matter most for a smaller operation into one conversation, sized to your business rather than copied from a large corporate programme.

Request a quoteSpeak to an advisor

General information only. What is covered, the terms and the premium depend on the insurer’s policy wording, your circumstances and the information you disclose. Nothing here is a promise of cover.

What it covers

  • Fire and allied perils on stock, equipment and fittings
  • Burglary and theft of stock and contents
  • Public liability for injury or damage to customers and visitors
  • Work injury cover for employees under WIBA
  • Money, goods in transit and equipment cover where relevant to how you trade

Who needs it

  • Retail shops and wholesalers
  • Restaurants, cafes and small hotels
  • Salons, clinics and small schools
  • Workshops and light manufacturers
  • Offices, agencies and service businesses

Common risks

One loss, no cushion

Smaller businesses rarely hold large reserves. An uninsured stock loss or liability claim can threaten the business itself.

Informal asset records

Stock and equipment values are often estimated. Keeping a simple asset list makes both quoting and claims easier.

Assuming the landlord covers it

A landlord’s policy normally covers the building, not your stock, fittings or your liability to customers.

Important considerations and exclusions

  • A package is only as good as its wording. Check what is excluded, the excess, and any security conditions such as alarms or guards.
  • Sums insured should reflect replacement value. A lower figure lowers the premium but can reduce a claim.
  • Not every insurer offers every extension to every type of business.

What affects the premium

  • Business type
  • Stock and equipment values
  • Premises and security
  • Employee numbers and payroll
  • Location
  • Claims history

Premiums are set by insurers, so we do not publish figures. Tell us about your situation and we will explain what is driving the quotation.

What we need for a quotation

  • Business type and trading address
  • Estimated stock and equipment values
  • Number of employees and rough annual payroll
  • Security arrangements (alarm, guards, shutters)
  • Existing cover and renewal date, if any

How Chestnut can help

We explain the cover in plain language, collect the information insurers need, approach suitable insurers for terms, and help with renewals and claims. Policies are issued by insurers, and you decide what to buy.

Frequently asked questions

Is SME insurance a single product?

Usually it is a package or a set of covers arranged together. What is included varies by insurer and by the type of business. We help you list what you need and then approach suitable insurers.

I run a one-person business. Do I still need cover?

If you hold stock, serve customers, or work from premises, some cover is usually sensible. If you employ anyone, work injury cover is generally a legal duty. We can help you separate what is required from what is advisable.
